paragraphs: Caution signal | This page corresponds to O*NET-SOC 53-7062.00 Laborers and Freight, Stock, and Material Movers, Hand. Official scope: manually move freight, stock, luggage, or other materials, or perform other general labor; includes general laborers not classified elsewhere (designated Bright Outlook). Typical tasks include picking and loading to orders, manually moving and stacking, counting and checking quantities, using hand trucks or pallet-moving tools, assisting mechanical loading and unloading, and keeping work areas clean and safe. Core deliverables are accurate, undamaged, timely handling and handover records, rather than merely moving things. Risks involve handling and ergonomic injuries, machinery and site safety, incorrect quantities and documents, severe weather and site conditions, and anomaly reporting. U.S. figures are BLS exact occupational data presented by O*NET (2024 employment 2,988,900; 2024—2034 projections 2%, average annual openings 384,300; 2025 median annual wage 40,240 USD; main industry transportation and warehousing). See the China pay section for evidence boundaries; regional quotes do not fill national figures. Difficulty with physical demands, outdoor work, and safety protection requirements represents practical costs to weigh seriously.

Responsibility assessment | Real fit comes from whether you can do three things within the same job: complete handling and handover properly (check item names and quantities against documents, move and stack according to labels and packaging requirements, use suitable hand or pallet tools, and complete signed handovers and records); manage safety and protection (wear protective equipment, follow machinery and vehicle-area rules, use ergonomic methods and aids, identify hazardous materials or damaged packaging, and stop and report); and accept definable job responsibilities (take responsibility for your handling quality, quantity checks, and safety behavior, and seek instructions for matters beyond authority or requiring machinery qualifications). Test this through a verifiable experience—checking Y's paper picking cards and draft handover without moving objects or operating equipment—rather than relying only on interest questionnaire conclusions.

Assessing fit | Use Y's fixed 20 cards to check 18 pending handover / 2 on hold, recalculate 43 and three trips of 20/20/3, check R's prohibition and Q's conditions, and revise the handover draft that was not actually dispatched; four work samples and a seven-day plan of 20—30 minutes daily appear in the pathway. Paper only, with no physical moving or trial equipment operation; this cannot determine physical eligibility.

Fit signals | O*NET 53-7062.00 work activities emphasize handling and moving objects, operating equipment and tools, obtaining information, collaborating with colleagues, and inspecting and checking. If you are willing to check quantities through procedures under physical demands and outdoor conditions, follow safety protection requirements, and make handovers and anomalies reviewable records, these daily demands are closer to your working style; interest and personality tools only help design trials, not determine hiring eligibility or performance.

Manually move freight, stock, luggage, and other materials, including general labor not separately classified. Check identity and quantities against documents, move and stack within safety and authority, hand over, and report anomalies. U.S. 2025 median annual wage is 40,240 USD; see the China pay section for wage evidence boundaries.

entries: Work objects | Freight, stock, luggage, and other materials, job documents and labels, handling tools and pallets, and loading sites and vehicle areas form the basis of handling within safety and authorization boundaries.

Checkable outputs | Reviewable picking and loading records, counts and quantity checks, signed handover evidence, damage or anomaly reports, and protective-equipment and site-safety behavior records; results must be traceable to documents and item labels.
Complete workflow | Receive work instructions → check documents and item labels → select handling tools and routes → load, stack, and recheck quantities → obtain signed handover and report anomalies.

paragraphs: Key judgments | O*NET work context reports: exactness or accuracy, 58% extremely important; repetitive tasks, 53% extremely important; constant contact with others, 57%; teamwork, 51% extremely important; decision frequency, 51% daily; task priorities and goals, 52% considerable freedom. Judgments rely on documents and labels, quantity checks, and safety protection and work-area rules. These are U.S. O*NET respondent distributions, not fixed conditions for all warehouses or Chinese jobs.

Environment and pace | Work mainly involves on-site physical labor: ordinary protective or safety equipment, 80% daily; outdoors in all weather, 76% daily; noise or distraction, 58% daily; workweek, 62% over 40 hours; standing, 23% continually; walking, 18% continually; time pressure, 46% at least weekly but not daily; decision freedom, 36% considerable freedom and 42% limited; dealing with unpleasant or angry people, 29% daily; controlled indoor environment, only 11% daily and 70% never. Loading plans, shifts, and project cycles drive the pace. These are U.S. O*NET respondent distributions, not fixed conditions for all warehouses or Chinese jobs.

Research inputs | Retain official RC; detail R84/C66/E17 gives intensities, not a basis for inventing RCE. Bright Outlook is an official designation, not an employment guarantee. U.S. BLS indicates typically no formal education requirement and short-term on-the-job training usually no longer than 1 month; O*NET Job Zone1—2 general descriptions indicate usually high school / equivalent, with some not requiring it, little experience through several months or a year, and training from days to a year, not uniform education or service for every job. Exact occupational 2025 industry distribution: transportation and warehousing 32%, administrative support 17%, manufacturing and wholesale each 14%, retail 12%; not industry wages or Chinese distribution. 2025 U.S. annual wage 10/25/50/75/90 percentiles are 31,270, 36,090, 40,240, 46,920, and 55,140 USD; official hourly wages are 15.03, 17.35, 19.35, 22.56, and 26.51 USD, respectively. Exact U.S. 53-7062 employment is 2,940,300 in 2025 and projected at 2,991,900 in 2035; 2025—2035 growth is 2%, with average annual openings of 340,500 (growth and replacement); net growth of 51,600 is not average annual openings.

This work first checks objects (freight and stock, documents and labels, handling tools and pallets, loading sites), inputs (work instructions and documents, item labels and packaging requirements, safety protection and work-area rules), and deliverables (picking and loading records, quantity checks, signed handover evidence, anomaly reports). Anything unverified remains pending verification; experience or intuition cannot replace document and label checks.

Work cycle | Check document identities and quantities → define tools and authority → move, review, and record under procedures → pause affected tasks for anomalies and report. For unknown leaks or unclear labels, stop affected handling, keep distance, and report; untrained people must not approach, move, repackage, or handle them independently. Isolation and emergency responses belong to trained, authorized personnel under institutional rules. In Chinese emergencies directly threatening personal safety, lawfully stop work or take possible measures then evacuate without waiting for instructions; paper Y involves no real shipment.

Adjacent-duty boundaries | This page covers only the exact O*NET-SOC 53-7062.00 occupation, Laborers and Freight, Stock, and Material Movers, Hand. Adjacent occupations such as shipping, receiving, and inventory clerks; weighers and measurers; construction laborers; extraction helpers; and machinery maintenance workers differ in work objects, qualifications, authority, and responsibility boundaries. They are not interchangeable based solely on titles, and proxy descriptions cannot replace employer training, machinery operating qualifications, and local safety laws.

Shipping, receiving, and inventory clerks | Core outputs are document processing, inventory records, and reconciliation of records with stock. This occupation mainly involves manual handling and loading; document and system duties differ, so titles alone do not make them interchangeable.

Weighers and measurers | Core outputs are weighing, measuring, and sampling records. This occupation mainly involves moving materials and checking quantities; measurement accuracy and record definitions differ and require separate checks.

Construction laborers | Core outputs are support and structural work at construction sites. This occupation mainly moves materials in warehouses and loading areas; site risks and work methods differ and cannot be applied interchangeably.

Extraction helpers | Core outputs are support tasks at extraction sites. This occupation generally works at warehousing, transportation, and production sites; high-risk-site qualifications and procedures differ and require separate checks.
Laborers and freight, stock, and material movers, hand: work objects and AI boundaries—which steps may receive assistance and which judgments must remain human responsibilities.

Conventional warehouse information systems, barcode checks, and mechanical automation differ from generative AI. BLS mentions conveyor sorting systems in some warehouses, not widespread generative AI adoption, efficiency gains, or replacement rates for this occupation. Generative AI may be tested for approved fictional record summaries / drafts, but outputs need checking against documents, physical items, authority, and site conditions; text outputs must not authorize handling, equipment operation, or hazard response.

Evidence note | ILO2025 global task exposure does not measure occupational adoption or efficiency gains; NIST's general generative AI risk framework supports preventing fabrication and verification. In unique U.S. job postings in 2025, Excel/Office each appear in 3%, SAP/Outlook each 2%, Word1%, and Edge/Safari/Firefox/OracleDB/AutoCAD each <1%; GoogleDocs has no percentage, which does not mean 0. Recruitment software mentions do not equal generative AI adoption.

Differences | Use Y to compare human and tool errors and time checking 18/2, 43, and 20/20/3; standardized text enables trial design, but unmeasured results cannot establish acceleration, and research does not establish that physical handling can never be automated.

Responsibility chain | From confirming work instructions and authorization through systems or equipment, human review, site work, and handover records, each step needs an identified responsible person and traceable evidence; system prompts cannot replace on-site safety confirmation and quantity checks.

Tool use | Complete Y manually first, then use approved tools to draft undispatched records and compare errors and time; without measurements, do not claim changed efficiency. Check site safety, item condition, and operating authority against actual systems.

Assistance trial | Use Y to organize card numbers, quantities, formulas, and undispatched drafts, retaining original materials and revisions; routes and safety conditions need actual confirmation, while software mentions do not establish autonomous dispatching or equipment adoption.

Human control points: check documents against physical items, confirm site safety conditions and record anomalies, and take responsibility for quantities, item condition, and work safety; equipment and system outputs cannot replace human confirmation.

OEWS covers employer-reported wages, including incentive pay but excluding overtime pay, nonproduction bonuses, and employer-paid benefits; percentiles are not starting pay, after-tax income, or individual quotes. Hourly wages are disclosed separately on the original page.

Interpretation | This scope helps explain occupational wage distribution and demand direction, but is not an individual quote and cannot be compared directly with mainland China or any other market; this large occupation spans many industries, and percentiles do not correspond to specific employers or shifts.

Industry scope | Exact occupational 2025 industry distribution: transportation and warehousing 32%, administrative support 17%, manufacturing and wholesale each 14%, retail 12%; not industry wages or Chinese distribution. Exact occupational industry wages were not obtained this round; industry wages on the combined BLS page cover multiple hand laborer and material mover occupations and do not apply to 53-7062.

Influencing factors | Industry and employer type, shifts (day, night, or rotating), piece rates or overtime, region, and union agreements affect actual income and stability; this page's percentiles are statistical positions, not specific jobs.

Which interests, abilities, and working styles matter more for laborers and freight, stock, and material movers, hand? This page discusses fit through work samples and responsibility boundaries only, without using personality labels to replace hiring eligibility or performance judgments.

Direct answer | Fit signals are willingness to check documents and quantities through on-site procedures, safety awareness under physical demands and outdoor conditions, reviewable handover and anomaly records, and stopping and reporting damage, hazardous materials, or safety hazards, rather than personality labels. Interest and personality tools only help design trials, not determine hiring eligibility or performance.

Positive signals | You can pick, move, and stack according to documents and labels; recheck quantities and correctly complete handover evidence; and wear required protective equipment and follow machinery and vehicle-area rules.

Caution conditions | Risk signals include incorrect quantities or labels, unstable stacking or overload, missing protective equipment, prohibited passage through vehicle or machinery areas, failure to stop and report damaged or hazardous packaging, and injuries from poor handling posture; difficulty with physical demands, outdoor work, and safety protection requirements represents practical costs to weigh seriously.

Paper trial | Y checks 20 ordered / 18 pending handover / 2 on hold, 43 simulated kg and three trips of 20/20/3, R's prohibition, no contact with unknown leaks, and correction of 'handed over'; four work samples and the seven-day plan appear in the pathway, without simulating real physical loads or equipment operation.

Conclusion | Activity preferences are closer to a Realistic and Conventional combination (O*NET interest code RC); interest codes only help design trials, not determine hiring eligibility or performance.

Personality boundaries | This round did not establish scale predictive validity for occupational performance; use Y quantities, identities, formulas, safety, and draft revisions to ask questions, without inferring performance, physical ability, or hiring from personality labels.

Conclusion | RIASEC or personality frameworks only help formulate questions; they cannot replace employer training, machinery operating qualifications, safety responsibilities, or evidence of actual work performance. No tool conclusion constitutes a hiring or qualification judgment.

Handling and ergonomic risk | Trigger: prolonged repetitive handling, poor posture, or exceeding individual capacity. Consequence: may cause musculoskeletal injuries and work interruptions. Controls: use pallet trucks and assistive tools, ergonomic handling methods, split loads or team handling when needed, and promptly report discomfort. Boundary: employer systems and local safety laws determine loads and work arrangements.

Machinery and site safety risk | Trigger: prohibited passage through vehicle or machinery areas, operating equipment without qualifications, excessive stacking height, or overload. Consequence: may cause injuries and cargo losses. Controls: follow work-area rules and warning signs, operate only equipment for which qualified, and stack properly and check stability. Boundary: employers and local rules determine equipment qualifications and site procedures.

Hazardous materials and damaged packaging risk | Damage, unknown leaks, or unclear labels may cause injuries and cargo losses. For unknown leaks or unclear labels, stop affected handling, keep distance, and report; untrained people must not approach, move, repackage, or handle them independently. Isolation and emergency responses belong to trained, authorized personnel under institutional rules. Evacuate under applicable systems when personal safety is directly threatened; waiting to report is not a reason to continue taking risks.

Quantity and document checking risk | Trigger: shipping or signing without checking documents and labels. Consequence: may cause misdeliveries, omissions, and discrepancies between records and stock. Controls: check quantities and labels item by item, use two-person checks for key items, and retain signed handover records. Boundary: employer systems determine checking and signing authority.

Severe weather and site condition risk | Trigger: extreme weather, slippery ground, or inadequate lighting during outdoor loading. Consequence: may cause slips, falls, and cargo damage. Controls: monitor weather and site conditions, pause and report when needed, and use suitable protection and lighting. Boundary: employer systems and local rules determine work pauses and protective requirements.

Preparation and training | U.S. BLS indicates typically no formal education requirement and short-term on-the-job training usually no longer than 1 month; O*NET Job Zone1—2 general descriptions indicate usually high school / equivalent, with some not requiring it, little experience through several months or a year, and training from days to a year, not uniform education or service for every job.

Entry checks | Check employer tasks, shifts, protection, training, equipment types, and authority; course certificates are not job licenses. Mile Human Resources and Social Security Bureau's fifth announcement, 2026-02-12: Yunnan Dazhongjiu Holding Group Co., Ltd. seeks several loaders at 3,600—4,000 yuan/month, with shuttle transport and meals; no specific education, shift, tasks, or deadline listed for this role. Current recruitment was not checked this round, so do not describe it as closed or a national threshold; the quote is not take-home income or national percentiles, and other roles' conditions are not imported.

Jurisdiction requirements | U.S. OSHA1910.178(l) requires formal and practical training, workplace competency evaluation, and employer certification records for covered powered industrial trucks, not a uniform external license for all movers. China's Work Safety Law requires passing safety education and training before work, with relevant qualifications for special operations; Article 14 of the Special Equipment Safety Law requires relevant personnel to obtain qualifications as prescribed. Neither classifies all manual handling as one licensed trade. Check the role, specific equipment, training, and work authorization. Report hazards immediately; workers may refuse unlawful instructions or forced risky work and, in emergencies directly threatening personal safety, lawfully stop work or take possible measures then evacuate without waiting for successive approvals.

Qualification boundaries | On-the-job training or short courses do not automatically grant machinery operating qualifications, hazardous-material handling authority, or work authorization; education, training, qualifications, hiring, and work authorization are different statuses, with specific requirements depending on employers and local rules.

Paper exercise Y | Entirely fictional, using only cards and formulas, without moving real heavy objects, operating vehicles, or touching chemicals. Order: A12 boxes and B8 boxes; on-site cards A01—A11 are labeled A and intact, while A12 is damaged with an unknown leak; B01—B07 are labeled B and intact, while B08 is labeled C with identity unverified. Simulated rules: Y1 only confirmed, intact items may be recorded as pending handover; Y2 stop affected handling for anomalies, keep distance, and report without touching leaks; Y3 each eligible A card is 2 simulated kg and B card 3 simulated kg, with the paper tool rated at 20 simulated kg per trip, not a human lifting limit or real equipment parameter. Route R is a vehicle work area prohibiting pedestrians; Q is marked as permitted and unobstructed in the simulation. The incorrect draft says '20 intact boxes handed over, one trip of 43 kg via R.' Task: review quantities, verification gaps, and anomalies, write a recalculable trip plan under Y1—Y3, choose a simulated route, and revise the handover draft; no real shipping or signing occurs.

Reference deliverables | Order: 20 boxes; confirmed and intact A11+B7=18 boxes pending handover, while leaking A12 and C-labeled B08 make 2 boxes on hold. Do not write 20 intact or handed-over boxes; B08 cannot be relabeled B based on the order. The 18 boxes weigh 11×2+7×3=43 simulated units; one trip of 43 exceeds the 20 rating by 23. At least 3 trips are needed: trip 1, A01—A10=20; trip 2, A11+B01—B06=2+18=20; trip 3, B07=3. Three trips cover 18 boxes and 43, each ≤20. This formula tests paper rules only, not physical load stability or human ability. Choose Q; R prohibits pedestrians, and real routes still require on-site safety checks. Under Y2, do not touch A12; report location / card number / visible leak without guessing the chemical; B08 identity remains unverified. Revise the draft to '18 boxes pending handover, 2 on hold for checking, a three-trip paper plan, not actually dispatched or signed for,' without inventing authority or signatures. Four work samples: card, quantity, and anomaly table; trip formulas and route checks; undispatched handover draft; anomaly report and authorization verification checklist.

Seven-day plan | 20—30 minutes daily: day 1 build 20 paper cards from Y; day 2 check 18 pending handover / 2 on hold and identity discrepancies; day 3 recalculate 43 and three trips of 20/20/3; day 4 check R's prohibition / Q's conditions and no contact with leaks; day 5 correct the false 'handed over'; day 6 ask a peer to cross-check only the four paper work samples and retain revisions; day 7 combine deliverables and separately check target job training, equipment, and authority. Paper samples do not measure physical ability, grant equipment qualifications, or replace safety training.

Transfer pathways | Before transitioning, list transferable abilities (document and quantity checking, site safety and protection, tool and equipment use, label and packaging identification, handovers and records), then identify qualifications and authorization evidence required for the new role; moving into shipping, receiving and inventory, weighing and measuring, machinery maintenance, or construction support requires each role's qualifications, record definitions, and safety procedures.

Machinery maintenance 49-9043 covers routine lubrication and part replacement, not all complex repair engineering. The final inventory reconciliation focus has the same target as the first item, not a sixth independent occupation.

risks.affected_roles: Laborers and freight, stock, and material movers, hand
risks.consequence: May cause musculoskeletal injuries and work interruptions.
risks.mitigation: Use pallet trucks and assistive tools, ergonomic handling methods, split loads or team handling when needed, and promptly report discomfort.
risks.scenario: Prolonged repetitive handling, poor posture, or exceeding individual capacity.

risks.affected_roles: Laborers and freight, stock, and material movers, hand
risks.consequence: May cause injuries and cargo losses.
risks.mitigation: Follow work-area, stacking, and load procedures; use equipment under applicable training, evaluation, qualification, and authorization, without requiring the same machinery certificate for all manual handling.
risks.scenario: Prohibited passage through vehicle or machinery areas, operating equipment without qualifications, excessive stacking height, or overload.

risks.affected_roles: Laborers and freight, stock, and material movers, hand
risks.consequence: May cause leaks, injuries, and compliance problems.
risks.mitigation: For unknown leaks or unclear labels, stop affected handling, keep distance, and report; untrained people must not approach, move, repackage, or handle them independently. Isolation and emergency responses belong to trained, authorized personnel under institutional rules.
risks.scenario: Moving packages without identifying damage, leaks, or unclear labels.

risks.affected_roles: Laborers and freight, stock, and material movers, hand
risks.consequence: May cause misdeliveries, omissions, and discrepancies between records and stock.
risks.mitigation: Check quantities and labels item by item, use two-person checks for key items, and retain signed handover records.
risks.scenario: Shipping or signing without checking documents and labels.

risks.affected_roles: Laborers and freight, stock, and material movers, hand
risks.consequence: May cause slips, falls, and cargo damage.
risks.mitigation: Monitor weather and site conditions, pause and report when needed, and use suitable protection and lighting.
risks.scenario: Extreme weather, slippery ground, or inadequate lighting during outdoor loading.

risks.affected_roles: Laborers and freight, stock, and material movers, hand
risks.consequence: May cause injuries and cargo losses.
risks.mitigation: For unknown leaks or unclear labels, stop affected handling, keep distance, and report; untrained people must not approach, move, repackage, or handle them independently. Isolation and emergency responses belong to trained, authorized personnel under institutional rules. In emergencies directly threatening personal safety, evacuate under applicable law and emergency systems without waiting for successive approvals.
risks.scenario: Continuing work despite quantity discrepancies, damaged goods, hazardous packaging, or site hazards.
